question: A DMSA scan is recommended to detect renal scarring following a first febrile UTI in an infant, while a micturating cystourethrogram (MCU) is used to detect vesico-ureteric reflux (VUR).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. DMSA (static renal scintigraphy) identifies cortical defects from scarring; MCU (voiding cystogram) documents VUR grade. Both are part of the standard imaging protocol after febrile UTI in infants.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. DMSA detects acute pyelonephritis and subsequent renal scarring; MCU confirms VUR. These are the two key imaging investigations after confirmed febrile UTI in young children.
